citations.description: Ticket comment (IMPLEMENTED AND PUSHED): 'So 200-with-new-key vs 301 vs 404 stays open, and I am recording that rather than picking the answer two research passes disagreed about.'

Ticket comment (LIVE DC HARNESS EVIDENCE): 'WHAT REMAINS UNSETTLED, unchanged and already documented on this ticket: a real project MOVE is not performable through pycontribs/jira 3.10.5... So what GET /issue/{oldKey} returns after a genuine move stays OPEN.'

findings.criterion: [operator-attested] what `GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey}` returns for a moved issue on DC 8.17.1 (status, and whether the body carries the new key) is RECORDED on this ticket as evidence — two research passes disagreed and the answer must stop being folklore.
findings.detail: The ticket explicitly records that this question remains UNSETTLED and cannot be answered on this harness: a project move is not performable through pycontribs/jira 3.10.5 (no move member), and DC's move is a UI wizard. The live harness evidence recorded (GitHub Actions run 30682512839, job 91322195258) covers resolution by numeric id and deletion behavior — not what a stale key returns after a genuine move. The criterion requires the status code (200/301/404) and whether the body carries the new key to be recorded; the ticket explicitly states '200-with-new-key vs 301 vs 404 stays open'. No concrete attestation of the specific outcome the criterion demands exists.
findings.remediation: Perform a real project move on a DC 8.17.1 instance (via the UI wizard or a test harness that can drive it), then record the HTTP status code and response body of GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey} as a ticket comment, naming the DC version, the old key, the new key, and the observed status/body. That comment is the attestation this criterion requires.
